hazards.control: Pressure test before opening to the well; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.

name: Subsurface safety valve
function: The fail-closed flapper valve in the tubing a few hundred feet below surface, held open by hydraulic control pressure from surface and closing on loss of that pressure.

tabs.overview: Required offshore and on some land wells near people or infrastructure. A control line from a wellhead panel holds a piston against a spring; losing pressure (a fire, a line break, or a manual trip) lets the flapper close on flow. Tubing-retrievable valves are part of the string; wireline-retrievable valves land in a nipple.
tabs.engineering: Per API Spec 14A; setting depth, closing time, and leak rate tested; control line rated to the setting pressure plus margin.
tabs.connections: In the tubing string; control line to the tree panel.
tabs.safety: Function tested on a schedule; the tree panel is part of the safety system.
tabs.evidence: API 6A scope for trees (S1), API Spec 14A for safety valves (S29), API 11D1 for packers (S21), field practice (S9). Photographs read for proportion only.
tabs.failure_modes: Flapper leaks, control line leaks, failure to close.

standards.paraphrase: Subsurface safety valve design validation and functional testing.
